analysis.title: Japan Electronic Components/Semiconductors: NVDA read-across: Strong earnings outlook and product roadmap provide reassurance
key_insights: NVDA FY27 3Q (Aug-Oct) revenue of US$115.8bn (+20% qoq) beat GSe of US$110.1bn, consensus of US$109.5bn and the guidance midpoint of US$108.0bn.
The Blackwell to Rubin transition is proceeding smoothly. Rubin platform sales were about US$20bn.
Non-GPU sales are expanding. Networking revenue was US$21.0bn and CPU revenue is expected to double in FY1/28.
NVDA is no longer shipping Hopper products to China.
NVDA guided 4Q (Nov-Jan) revenue to US$130.0bn at the midpoint, above GSe and consensus of US$124.8bn. The FY1/28 revenue growth outlook was raised from 70% to 75%.
Product launch schedule is on plan: Vera Rubin Ultra in 2027, Feynman in 2028.
NVDA shares were up about 4.5% after hours as of 18:00 local time.
GS says the results match the robust outlook seen from the Asian upstream supply chain and should reassure the Asian AI-related supply chain.
GS has Buy ratings on five passive and ceramic component names (Murata Mfg, Taiyo Yuden, TDK, Nichicon, MARUWA) that left a highly positive impression with 1H FY3/27 results.
Ibiden: GS awaits clarity on the outlook for its yet-to-be-finalized new plant construction and assumes funding from customers including NVDA, based on prior capacity expansions. GS maintains Buy.
In analog/power, Rohm has larger NVDA-related exposure via Taiwanese power supply makers. Renesas is seeing substantial PMIC expansion for ASICs in addition to NVDA. GS maintains Buy on both.

market_movers.rationale: Murata Mfg. 12-month target based on FY3/29E EV/GCI vs CROCI/WACC with an 80% premium to the sector multiple of 10X, implying FY3/29E P/E of 29X.
Taiyo Yuden target based on FY3/29E EV/GCI vs CROCI/WACC with an 80% premium to the 10X sector multiple, implying FY3/29E P/E of 30X.
TDK target based on FY3/29E EV/GCI vs CROCI/WACC with a 10% premium to the sector average EV/DACF multiple of 10X, implying FY3/29E P/E of 26X.
Nichicon target based on FY3/29E EV/GCI vs CROCI/WACC, implying FY3/28E P/E of 22X.
MARUWA target based on FY28E EBITDA with a 12.2X multiple derived from the historical correlation between EBITDA margin and EV/EBITDA.
Ibiden target based on FY3/29E EV/GCI vs CROCI/WACC with a 60% premium to the sector average EV/DACF multiple of 10X, implying FY3/29E P/E of 41X. GS awaits clarity on new plant plans.
Rohm target based on FY3/29E EV/GCI vs CROCI/WACC with a 20% premium to the sector-average EV/DACF multiple of 10X, implying FY3/29E P/E of 23X. Exposure to NVDA via Taiwanese power supply makers.

Renesas target based on FY12/28E EV/GCI vs CROCI/WACC with an EV/DACF multiple of 13X, a 30% premium to the sector average, implying FY12/27E P/E of 16X. PMIC demand for ASICs is expanding beyond NVDA.

sector_views.rationale: NVDA's results and outlook, and the on-plan product shifts and launches, should reassure the Asian AI-related supply chain. GS is Buy on all eight covered names in the note.

earnings_insights: NVDA FY27 3Q (Aug-Oct) reported revenue US$115.8bn (+20% qoq) vs GSe US$110.1bn, consensus US$109.5bn and guidance midpoint US$108.0bn, reported 11/18 JST.
NVDA 4Q (Nov-Jan) revenue guidance midpoint US$130.0bn vs GSe US$124.8bn and consensus US$124.8bn (estimates, guidance given 11/18).
NVDA reported networking revenue of US$21.0bn and Rubin platform sales of about US$20bn in 3Q.
NVDA FY1/28 revenue growth outlook raised from 70% to 75%. CPU revenue is expected to double in FY1/28.
GS notes 1H FY3/27 results of Murata Mfg, Taiyo Yuden, TDK, Nichicon and MARUWA left a highly positive impression.
risk_factors: Murata Mfg: decline in smartphone production volume, deterioration in MLCC supply/demand, yen appreciation.
Taiyo Yuden: weaker-than-expected smartphone demand, MLCC supply/demand deterioration, yen appreciation.
TDK: decline in smartphone production volume, higher input costs, yen appreciation.

Nichicon: high share price volatility as an AI-related small- and mid-cap stock, quarterly earnings volatility, rising raw material and electricity costs, reduced subsidies for storage battery products.

MARUWA: lower investment in applications supporting final demand (AI/general-purpose servers, xEV, SPE), lower end-product demand from supply chain disruptions and inventory adjustments, emergence of alternative technology.
Ibiden: roadmap changes at main customers, weaker PC and server demand, lower diesel vehicle sales.

Rohm: further increases in precious metal prices, delays in business portfolio transformation, uncertainty around potential reorganization and integration, fluctuations in the market valuation of Toshiba shares.

Renesas: slowdown or delayed recovery in consumer electronics demand, stagnant automobile production, protracted semiconductor inventory reduction, delayed recovery in industrial equipment demand, yen appreciation.
geopolitical: NVDA is no longer shipping Hopper products to China.
